chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When the Tala'a (evaporated grape juice) exceeds one-third, it is prohibited.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on grape juice residue when it exceeds one-third?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the boundary between *khamr* (intoxicant) and *nabidh* (non-intoxicant grape residue) by establishing that exceeding one-third concentration renders it haram, a key criterion in Shia fiqh for determining intoxication levels. The ruling reflects the scholarly consensus on how evaporation increases potency, linking physical transformation to ritual purity and consumption laws. It serves as a practical guideline for distinguishing permissible fermented drinks from those that induce intoxication.
